subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt provider-level persisted cooldown identity for inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials, including the `inline-api-key:<provider>` usage namespace and fail-closed behavior during billing/auth windows?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes provider credential selection, persistence, and upgrade behavior for existing inline-key users, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Accept Provider-Level Cooldown
options.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys get billing/auth cooldown protection while healthy stored profiles remain usable fallback credentials.

options.title: Keep Profile-Only Cooldowns
options.body: Document auth profiles as the supported cooldown boundary and keep inline keys outside cooldown tracking.

options.title: Request Narrower Design
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers define the exact inline credential identity, persistence, and recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept Provider-Level Cooldown
recommendation.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys get billing/auth cooldown protection while healthy stored profiles remain usable fallback credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: The model config/auth-profile redesign and recent SecretRef auth work make steipete the best available owner for the product and compatibility decision.
